samples.summary: `addSlide` accepts any `layoutId` because `MemSlidesStore` never rejects one — `getLayout` silently falls back to `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS[0]`, so a typo'd layout returns 200 and stores a slide whose `layoutId` names a layout that does not exist
samples.evidence: `packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:196-198`: `export function getLayout(layoutId: string): Layout { return BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS.find(l => l.id === layoutId) ?? BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS[0]; }` — no throw. `MemSlidesStore.resolveLayout` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:172-174) resolves the deck's own layouts first and then delegates there, and `addSlide` (memory.ts:176-227) writes `layoutId` onto the new slide verbatim. `ApiV1SlidesController.add` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/slides.controller.ts:100-105) only checks the value is a non-empty string, so `POST .../slides {"layoutId":"titel-body"}` answers 200 with a title-slide body and persists a dangling `layoutId` that the editor's own `applyLayout`/renderer will later resolve to a different layout again. The fix belongs on the new code: resolve `layoutId` against `document.layouts` ∪ `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS` (the list `listLayouts` already builds) and 400 on a miss.

samples.summary: `duplicateTab` copies only three of `TabMeta`'s six optional fields — `lakehouseSourceId`, `lakehouseRef` and `asOf` are silently dropped from the copy
samples.evidence: `TabMeta` is declared at `packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:121-131` with `kind`, `datasourceId`, `query`, `lakehouseSourceId`, `lakehouseRef` and `asOf`; `duplicateTab` carries only the first three. The dropped fields are exactly what the editor reads to render such a tab — `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/lakehouse-view.tsx:74` (`tab?.lakehouseSourceId`) and :76 (`tab?.asOf`) — so a duplicate of a `lakehouse` tab would be a `type: 'lakehouse'` tab pointing at nothing. Today the `no worksheet → 400` check in `tabs.controller.ts:255-261` keeps external tabs out of this path (datasource/lakehouse tabs occupy a `tabOrder` slot with no `sheets` entry — see the note at packages/frontend/src/components/history/__tests__/revision-preview.test.tsx:385-387), so it is latent rather than reachable; it becomes a broken tab the moment an external tab gains a materialized worksheet. Copying the whole `TabMeta` minus `id`/`name` would be robust to the next field added to that type.

finding.evidence: `packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:196-198`: `export function getLayout(layoutId: string): Layout { return BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS.find(l => l.id === layoutId) ?? BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS[0]; }` — no throw. `MemSlidesStore.resolveLayout` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:172-174) resolves the deck's own layouts first and then delegates there, and `addSlide` (memory.ts:176-227) writes `layoutId` onto the new slide verbatim. `ApiV1SlidesController.add` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/slides.controller.ts:100-105) only checks the value is a non-empty string, so `POST .../slides {"layoutId":"titel-body"}` answers 200 with a title-slide body and persists a dangling `layoutId` that the editor's own `applyLayout`/renderer will later resolve to a different layout again. The fix belongs on the new code: resolve `layoutId` against `document.layouts` ∪ `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS` (the list `listLayouts` already builds) and 400 on a miss.

verdict.reason: The finding's load-bearing claim — that MemSlidesStore.addSlide "writes `layoutId` onto the new slide verbatim" and so "persists a dangling `layoutId`" — is not what the code does. packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:178 resolves the layout (`const layout = this.resolveLayout(layoutId)`) and line 189 stamps `layoutId: layout.id`, i.e. the RESOLVED layout's id. An unknown id falls back through resolveLayout (memory.ts:172-174) to getLayout (packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:196-198) to BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS[0], and the slide is persisted with layoutId 'blank' — never with an id naming a nonexistent layout. The claimed downstream consequence ("the editor's own applyLayout/renderer will later resolve to a different layout again") therefore cannot occur; applyLayoutToSlide also writes the resolved id (layout.ts:402). Two supporting details are also wrong: BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS[0] is 'blank' (layout.ts:65-71), not a title slide, so a typo yields an empty blank slide rather than "a title-slide body"; and emptyDocument seeds layouts: clone(BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS) (memory.ts:127), so the proposed document.layouts ∪ BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS set is normally just the built-ins. What genuinely remains is that slides.controller.ts:100-108 accepts any non-empty string and returns 200 with a blank slide instead of 400 — a validation-strictness point statable entirely from the diff, with no other call site broken, no guard bypassed, and no cross-module invariant violated (the stored deck stays internally consistent). That belongs to the correctness/design-fit lenses, not blast-radius.

finding.summary: `duplicateTab` copies the worksheet verbatim, so the copy's charts (and its `pivotTable`) still carry `sourceTabId` pointing at the ORIGINAL tab. `chart-utils.ts` resolves chart data with `root.sheets[chart.sourceTabId]`, so every chart on the duplicated tab renders the source tab's numbers, not the copy's — and a duplicated pivot output tab silently becomes a second dependent that makes the new `resolveDelete` refuse to delete the source tab, naming a tab the user never configured.
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/chart-utils.ts:116 `const sourceSheet = root.sheets[chart.sourceTabId];` (same at :188 and :281), and packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/pivot/use-pivot-table.ts:135 `const sourceWs = root.sheets[definition.sourceTabId];`. The new duplicate writes `const copy: Worksheet = { ...worksheet, comments: {} }` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/tab-ops.ts, duplicateTab) — chart ids and `sourceTabId`/`pivotTable.sourceTabId` are not remapped to the new tab id. Fix belongs in `duplicateTab`.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. `duplicateTab` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/tab-ops.ts:167-168) writes `{ ...worksheet, comments: {} }` into `root.sheets[newTabId]`, clearing only comments; `Worksheet` carries `charts` (worksheet-document.ts:88-90, with `SheetChart.sourceTabId` at :20) and `pivotTable` (:99), so both are copied with `sourceTabId` still pointing at the ORIGINAL tab. Consumers outside the diff resolve data by that field, not by the owning tab: chart-utils.ts:116, :188, :281 all `root.sheets[chart.sourceTabId]`, and use-pivot-table.ts:135 `root.sheets[definition.sourceTabId]` — so charts on the copy render the source tab's grid and never track edits made in the copy. The pivot consequence is also real: resolveDelete (tab-ops.ts:85-92) scans every tab's `pivotTable.sourceTabId` and refuses with `pivot_dependents`, and the frontend cascade at document-detail.tsx:515/:555 uses the same predicate, so a duplicated pivot output tab becomes an extra dependent. No guard makes this unreachable: the sole caller, tabs.controller.ts:238-271, validates only document type and worksheet existence, and duplicateTab deliberately copies `source.kind` (:162), including `pivot`. Existing tests (tab-ops.spec.ts:178-213) cover name/order/cells/comments only. This is in-lane for blast radius — pre-existing reader sites outside the diff rely on an invariant the new producer violates — and major by impact (wrong data rendered; a delete path that refuses on an auto-created dependent). The repo's own `duplicateSlide` (yorkie-slides-store.ts:739-749) remaps ids on duplication for exactly this reason.

finding.summary: `copyThread` detaches the anchor with the generic `detachYorkieValue`, but a docs-range anchor's `posRange` is explicitly documented as a value that does not survive a generic detach. `GET /comments` on a `doc` document therefore returns a `posRange` made of Yorkie CRDT metadata instead of a usable `TreePosStructRange`, so an API consumer cannot resolve or round-trip a docs thread anchor.
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/yorkie-comment-store.ts:81-88 states the invariant: "`posRange` is deliberately left as-is. Stored as a Yorkie array, its `toJSON()` returns a string-escaped serialization that does not round-trip through `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))`" — and this branch's own `yorkie-json.ts:13-20` warns that `detachYorkieValue` branches on `Array.isArray`, which is false for a Yorkie array proxy, so it returns `{createdAt, movedAt}` metadata. `copyThread` uses exactly that helper on `t.anchor`, and the comments controller's `list`/`setResolved`/`reply` return its output for `doc` documents.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. comment-ops.ts:99 does pass the whole anchor through detachYorkieValue, whose Array.isArray branch (yorkie-json.ts:172) is documented in this very branch (yorkie-json.ts:13-20) and in worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:65-70 as returning {createdAt, movedAt} CRDT metadata for a Yorkie array proxy. A docs anchor's posRange is a TreePosStructRange array (frontend/src/types/comments.ts:28-33) written straight into the CRDT by yorkie-comment-store.ts:164-187, whose own comment (lines 77-88) says it must never be re-serialised. The doc read path is live proxies, not a JSON snapshot: comments.controller.ts:250-257 calls listThreads(doc.getRoot().comments) and yorkie.service.ts:36-57 supplies a real yorkie.Document. setResolved/reply return the same copyThread output (comments.controller.ts:599). No guard or docs-specific anchor handling exists in the backend (posRange appears there only in prose), and the POST refusal at comments.controller.ts:276-289 only blocks creation, not reads of editor-created threads. Real, reachable wrong-result site violating an invariant another module documents and depends on.
